newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Horse Racing-Rivals fear Ireland's Oscar Schindler.
newsitem.headline: Horse Racing-Rivals fear Ireland's Oscar Schindler.

text.p: Australia's top trainers fear Irish raider Oscar Schindler will outpace and outlast any horse they have to offer in next week's Melbourne Cup classic.
The giant chestnut, winner of the Irish St Leger and a fast-finishing third to Helissio in this month's Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe, arrived in Australia a week ago and looks in superb pre-race form.
"I think the Irish horse has just got 50 lengths on the Australian and New Zealand horses -- I think Oscar Shindler is the horse to beat," said leading Australian trainer Gai Waterhouse.
Oscar Schindler, already a 3-1 favourite, heads the overseas challenge for the A$2.2 million (US$1.74 million) race over 3.2 kms (two miles) at Flemington on Tuesday.

Named after a German industrialist who saved more than 1,000 Polish Jews from Nazi death camps in World War Two, the horse was given a riding weight of 56.5kg when the handicappers set the weights for the 24-horse race in September.
Since then, the four-year-old has won the Irish Leger and challenged strongly in the Arc, Europe's richest race.
"He (Oscar Schindler) is the best performed horse to come out from the Britain for the Melbourne Cup," Cummings added.

Australian-trained Doriemus, second favourite at 11-2, will carry top weight of 58kg as he attempts to repeat his win last year. Two other horses -- Grey Shot and Court Of Honour -- have travelled to Australia from Britain to race in Melbourne.
Three years ago, Irish stayer Vintage Crop became the first horse trained outside Australasia to win the Melbourne Cup.
Irish big race specialist Michael Kinane, who partnered Vintage Crop in 1993, will ride the favourite next Tuesday.
Latest odds: Oscar Schindler 3-1, Doriemus 11-2, Nothin' Leica Dane and Senator 7-1, Saintly 8-1, Grey Shot 15-1, The Bandette 16-1, Court of Honour 20-1

"We work hard all year to work towards this Cup then get an outsider (overseas horse) thrown into the race, getting in under the handicap," Waterhouse was quoted as saying in Sydney's Daily Telegraph newspaper on Wednesday.
"What local horse could have run third in the Arc de Triomphe, you tell me? I don't think one of them could."
Waterhouse, who is pinning her Cup hopes on third favourite Nothin' Leica Dane, was supported by colleague Bart Cummings.
"I would say that he should have got another 2.5kg to 3.0kg," said Cummings, who is seeking his tenth Melbourne Cup success with 8-1 shot Saintly.
